prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy proteins, from the PROTAC concept to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type degraders.

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation is the opening choice I still find strongest, and three other members (Aili, Chabes, and in part Somfai and Zou) place it high. The idea is conceptually original: instead of occupying an active site, a small molecule brings a ubiquitin ligase to a target and uses the cell's own proteasome machinery, which extends pharmacology to proteins without conventional pockets. It is chemically clear (linker, E3 ligand and ternary-complex design), has been reproduced by many independent groups over two decades, and has a large clinical pipeline. The Crews/Deshaies PROTAC concept plus Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target covers both the engineered heterobifunctional line and the molecular-glue mechanism, which is the best way I see to fit a coherent story into three names.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim all have serious claims, and any three-person cut leaves out someone whose contribution was decisive. No degrader is yet approved, so the clinical proof of broad benefit is still pending, and a committee that wants a mature therapeutic outcome could reasonably wait. If the attribution cannot be defended, B027 (Car and Parrinello) is the cleaner prize, with an unambiguous two-author credit and four decades of confirmation.

responses.point: Somfai ranks B014 fourth, calling the credit entangled for a three-person cap and the field possibly premature since no PROTAC drug is approved, though the molecular-glue part is better established.
responses.response: I accept the entanglement but not the prematurity. The mechanistic validation (ternary complexes, cereblon biology, catalytic turnover) is mature and independent of whether a particular drug is approved; Nobel chemistry has not usually waited for approvals when the principle is established. Where I agree with Somfai is that the glue line is the more settled half, which is why I keep Handa in the set rather than Ciulli.

responses.point: Zou proposes the same Crews/Deshaies/Handa trio but notes this is a compound discovery in which PROTACs and glues might need separate recognition, and that late-stage trials without approval suggest it is slightly early.
responses.response: This is the most serious qualification and I share it. I would resist splitting it into two parts, because that forces a four-person union beyond the cap or drops one lineage entirely, and the shared principle of induced proximity to an E3 ligase is what makes it one achievement. A single citation worded around induced degradation covers both lines, but I accept that Zou's concern is unresolved if the committee insists on crediting Ciulli.

responses.point: Linke ranks Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first, arguing the two-author credit is unambiguous, the use is four decades old, and computational chemistry has had few recent recognitions.
responses.response: I agree on merit and attribution, and B027 is my second choice and first alternative. My reservation is the 2013 prize for multiscale modelling and the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction, which have both recently gone to computational work. I also have to say that this is my own field, so I am wary of favouring it over a clearly new modality. I would support it if the committee finds B014 attribution unworkable.

responses.point: Brzezinski places Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling first, valuing its mechanistic clarity and daily use in synthesis, while noting the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make the committee cautious.
responses.response: The impact is undeniable and the two-person credit is cleaner than for B014. My difficulty is the closeness to the 2010 prize for Pd-catalysed C-C coupling, so it reads as an extension of a recognised principle, whereas degradation introduces a new one. I regard B046 as strong enough that I would not oppose it, but I would not put it ahead of B014 unless the attribution problem there proves unresolvable.

responses.point: Aili ranks B014 first with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex rationale complete the PROTAC lineage, while leaving the cereblon line as a parallel unresolved allocation.
responses.response: This is the main alternative trio. Ciulli's contribution to structure-based ligand design is important and I would not call Handa's claim stronger on scientific merit alone. I choose Handa because the cereblon-thalidomide mechanism explains a drug used for decades and underlies molecular glues, giving the prize a broader scope, but I would be willing to discuss Ciulli in round 2 if colleagues think the PROTAC engineering line deserves more weight than the glue mechanism.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli is the better third name beside Crews and Deshaies, and whether Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are left out unfairly.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader drug makes the prize premature for a majority of the committee.
Whether Car-Parrinello (B027) should take priority given the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes.
statement.conflict_note: I was a postdoc with Arieh Warshel (2013 laureate, EVB), and B027 lies in my own field of computational chemistry, so my views on it deserve discounting. No specific personal or institutional connection to the B014 candidates is apparent from the provided profile.
